policy: This graph records where catalogue entries, observations, title-chain rows, working parcel-model events and nomenclature indexes cite or describe entities. A citation link is not proof of the proposition in the cited analysis. No person is merged by surname alone. BP Properties, BP Pension Trust, BP Trustees and the BP pension fund are distinct. Tŷ Mawr, Llandough Farm and Great House Farm near Cowbridge are distinct places. No ownership or boundary is inferred from a tithe/rate-book column, a recital, a catalogue heading, a family account or a shared place-name. Every relationship retains its source record, assertion basis, verification state and an explanatory source pinpoint.

entities.preferred_name: Parcel A — north woods plus house and garden
entities.notes: Working parcel-model slot only; not a verified title boundary or surveyed polygon. Current working model: Parcel A comprises A1 (the north woods) and A2 (the house, buildings and garden). The green south of the house is outside Parcel A. The 1928 family understanding of freehold is a testimony-based interpretation to test against the 1877 arrangement and Thomas estate/probate records. Limits: Analytical reconstruction, not yet a surveyed boundary. The 1877 instrument and plan remain essential to confirming extent and title.

Working parcel-model slot only; not a verified title boundary or surveyed polygon. The current model places the woods north of Mary Williams’s house within Parcel A as A1. The family/working account associates this ground with a 1955 taking, but the original order, writ, execution return and 1961 woodland deed must be compared before fixing the legal or physical extent. Limits: Do not assume that the wording “whole farm” proves that the order included A1; distinguish the order’s target from what was physically taken.

Working parcel-model slot only; not a verified title boundary or surveyed polygon. The farmhouse, buildings and garden are analysed as A2, the house part of Parcel A. The family’s reported 1928 freehold understanding and the later separate registration of the farmhouse are central to the current theory. Limits: The exact instrument, boundary, legal effect of the 1928 event and the relevant 1982–83 registration file remain to be verified. Alfred Thomas’s death is dated 14 December 1927 by the Dictionary of Welsh Biography, which creates a date/payee discrepancy with Mary Williams’s recollection of a 1928 payment “to Alfred Thomas”. Payment to an executor, estate or agent, a receipt still naming Alfred, or a remembered date/payee error are possibilities, not findings. The reported Cardiff Corporation bequest remains a secondary, unofficial press transcription; the will and grant have not been inspected, and no Llandough land transfer to the Corporation is established.

Working parcel-model slot only; not a verified title boundary or surveyed polygon. The current interpretation treats Parcel B as the eastern/right-hand agricultural fields covered by the 1939 WGR–John Williams tenancy plan and as the intended subject of the 1955 Order 14 action. Limits: The later phrase “whole farm” is ambiguous in this reconstruction. The original order and execution return are needed to establish its extent and what was taken. The allegation that the 1939 agreement was fraudulent remains unproven.

entities.preferred_name: Parcel C — green south of the house
entities.notes: Working parcel-model slot only; not a verified title boundary or surveyed polygon. The green south of Mary Williams’s house is treated as a separate parcel, Parcel C, outside Parcel A. The possibility that Williams held title or a possessory interest in C is an open question, not an established fact. Limits: Check the village-green VG41 application and map, the 1955 writ/return and relevant conveyances. Do not fold C back into Parcel A.
